title: They nailed Him to wood…
paragraphs:
They nailed Him to wood…
and somehow we turned it into buildings, brands, and boundaries.
Pause.
Did Jesus come to build a religion?
No.
But He did say something that shakes the ground beneath that question:
“I will build My church…” — Matthew 16:18
So what did He mean?

Not a system.
Not an institution.
Not a checklist of rituals to earn God.

The word He used for church was “ekklesia” — a called-out people.
Not walls.
People.
Living. Breathing. Broken people.

Like you.
Like me.
Here’s where we miss it—

Religion says: Clean yourself, then come.
Jesus says: Come, and I’ll make you clean.

Religion builds ladders to heaven.
Jesus brought heaven down—through His blood, through His cross.
And yes, over time, people organized. Structures formed. Traditions grew. Some beautiful. Some… heavy.
Some scholars interpret that the early followers naturally gathered into communities with leaders and practices (see Acts 2). That’s not wrong.
But hear this clearly:

Jesus didn’t die to create a system you perform for.
He died to restore a relationship you were made for.

The “church” He builds is not made of concrete.
It’s made of redeemed hearts.

People who were addicts.
Liars.
Broken.
Ashamed.

Now forgiven.
Now free.
Now alive in Him.
And the center is not rules.
It’s Jesus.

Crucified.
Risen.
Calling your name.

So if what you’ve seen feels like cold religion—
don’t walk away from Christ because of what man built around Him.
Run to Him.

He’s still building His church.
One transformed life at a time.
Including yours.

If this stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
This might be your moment to stop performing… and start surrendering.
